title: Men Are From Mars, Women Are From Venus

questions.q: After Mary vents about a difficult day at work, what does the summary say she actually needs from Tom?
a: To listen without jumping in with fixes
To suggest a practical plan of action
To give her space until she calms down
To share a similar story from his own job
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes Mary wanting Tom to listen, while Tom's instinct is to offer solutions.

questions.q: According to the summary, what makes a man feel motivated in a relationship?
a: Feeling useful and trusted by his partner
Being told exactly how to help out
Receiving frequent verbal reassurance
Spending more time talking about feelings
questions.why: Lesson 2 says men are motivated when they feel useful, while women are inspired when they feel loved.

questions.q: What does the summary say a woman usually means when she says the couple never goes out together?
a: She feels he has not paid attention to her lately
She literally means they have never gone out
She wants him to plan a specific trip for them
She is comparing him with other couples she knows
questions.why: Lesson 3 explains that 'never' expresses a feeling rather than a literal count of outings.

questions.q: How does the summary advise a woman to take a man's statement that he is fine?
a: Literally, and let him work things out alone
As a hint that she should keep asking
As a sign he is hiding a serious problem
As a request for several possible solutions
questions.why: Lesson 3 says men are often literal and will ask for help or solutions when they want them.

questions.q: What caution does the summary add about the book's portrait of men and women?
a: Individuals vary, so the patterns are not absolute
The differences disappear once couples marry
Only couples in therapy fit these patterns
The advice applies mainly to older generations
questions.why: The review says every individual is unique and the book should not be taken as absolute truth.
